input: The delivery in question is now running some 4 weeks late against the programme, and the delay in this case sits firmly with the supplier. The supplier's fabrication start was pushed back by a backlog of work at its own works, and the finished delivery date moved backwards by the same amount, because the fabrication itself was not shortened to recover the lost start. Nothing in this delay originates on the project side: the drawings were released on the dates the programme required, and no change to the item has been instructed since then. The activities due to take the item on arrival are therefore the activities at risk, and it is the float behind them that the delay will consume. The mitigation proposed in response is a resequencing of the installation works that follow the delivery. The project board is the owner of this mitigation. Under the resequencing, the installation crews would take first the work that does not depend on the delayed item, and the item would be installed on arrival into a programme cleared around it, so the late delivery is absorbed by work that was always going to be done rather than by work left waiting. The cost of the resequencing is essentially the cost of the changed order itself, in remobilisation and in supervision, and that cost is carried against the delay. Whether the resequencing manages to recover the whole of the delay will depend on how much of the following work can genuinely be advanced, and that judgement will be made when the revised programme is issued. The position reported at this stage is the position before that programme: a delay of 4 weeks at the supplier, a mitigation in preparation, and no recovery banked as yet.
